title: The Hidden Sponsor Thread
description: A harder case built around duplicate badges, staged logins, shell vendors, and a frame job designed to make the wrong suspect look guilty.

answerKey.method: She used a duplicate staff badge to move Lena’s emergency kit and staged Owen’s login to frame him.
answerKey.motive: She needed to hide sponsor money routed through Bayou Night Logistics, a shell vendor tied to her apartment mailbox.
answerKey.keyEvidence: Duplicate badge movement, shell vendor ledger, office-terminal metadata, and the recovered emergency kit defeat the Owen frame.
answerKey.explanation: Owen’s login looked guilty until Forensics proved it was used from a finance terminal while Owen’s phone was visible at the bar. The duplicate badge moved with the emergency kit, and the shell vendor points back to Marisol.

phone.title: Recovered Phone Analysis: Stationary Device
phone.text: Marisol’s phone stayed still near the finance desk while the duplicate badge moved through the office hall.
phone.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

messages.title: Message Extraction Report: Vendor Sheet Warning
messages.text: Lena messaged Marisol: “The second vendor sheet does not match the sponsor deck. I need the real version tonight.”
messages.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

maps.title: Location Analysis: Badge Path
maps.text: The duplicate badge path runs finance desk → office → service hall → linen cart alcove during the blackout window.
maps.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

bank.title: Financial Records Review: Bayou Night Logistics
bank.text: Sponsor deposits route through Bayou Night Logistics, a vendor using Marisol’s apartment mailbox.
bank.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

bank.title: Final Financial Summary: Shell Vendor Motive
bank.text: The hidden vendor ledger, mailbox link, and finance terminal metadata show the sponsor theft was Marisol’s operation.
bank.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

photos.title: Photo / Video Review: Owen Visible at Bar
photos.text: A guest photo shows Owen at the bar while his login is active on an office computer.
photos.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

contacts.title: Suspect Statement: Marisol Vega
contacts.text: Marisol says she never left finance and that Owen was the only person with enough access to stage the sponsor files.

contacts.title: Suspect Statement: Owen Landry
contacts.text: Owen says his login must have been used while he was on the bar floor because he never returned to the office during the blackout.

contacts.title: Suspect Statement: Tessa Marchand
contacts.text: Tessa says she saw Marisol near the linen cart earlier, holding a folder she folded shut when Lena approached.

contacts.title: Suspect Statement: Brielle Fox
contacts.text: Brielle says Marisol told her not to send the second vendor sheet until “the sponsor confusion” was fixed.

contacts.title: Suspect Statement: Cole Darden
contacts.text: Cole says the finance desk monitor showed a badge-audit screen before Marisol hurried back to close it.

notes.title: Physical Evidence Report: Emergency Kit Location
notes.text: Lena’s emergency kit is recovered behind a folded linen cart along the duplicate badge path.
notes.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

files.title: Document / Metadata Review: Duplicate Badge Export
files.text: A deleted badge-audit export shows a duplicate credential created under Marisol’s finance permissions.
files.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

files.title: Document / Metadata Review: Staged Login Terminal
files.text: Metadata shows Owen’s login was used from a finance-desk terminal, not from Owen’s office workstation.
files.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

browser.title: Browser History Review: Badge Audit Search
browser.text: A finance-desk browser searched how to clone a staff badge audit export and how long deleted exports remain recoverable.
browser.source: Recovered from the scene and processed by Forensics.

openingNarration: This case is not about the loudest suspect. Forensics has recovered badge data, financial records, device records, and deleted exports. Interrogate the suspects, build the Timeline, and use Deduction to test the frame.
revealScript: Marisol built the frame to make Owen look like the sponsor thief and the killer. But the duplicate badge kept moving while her phone stayed still, Owen’s login was used from the wrong terminal, and the shell vendor’s mailbox led back to her.
